items.title: Turn threat intelligence into informed action with Microsoft Defender
items.summary: Every new threat raises a familiar set of questions. Is it targeting our industry? Are we exposed? What should we investigate first? Answering those questions takes more than another feed or a longer list of indicators. It takes intelligence that brings the relevant context together and helps your team understand which threats matter to your organization and where to investigate next. With the new Threat Intelligence experience in Microsoft Defender , we're bringing Microsoft threat intelligence, third-party sources, and your team's own insights together around the way you work. Threat Intelligence Overview helps you prioritize the threats most relevant to your organization. Threat Intelligence Explorer gives analysts a centralized experience to search, filter, and investigate the intelligence behind them. Focus on the threats that matter to your organization A threat can be significant globally without being your team's most urgent concern. Your industry, the regions where you operate, and what's happening in your environment all shape what deserves attention. Threat Intelligence Overview puts that context at the center of your starting page. The personalized dashboard brings the external threat landscape together with insights about your organization, highlighting relevant threats, their impact, and your exposure. You can focus on industries and regions of interest, see threats actively affecting your organization, and identify where a closer investigation is needed. For an analyst planning the day's research or a security leader reviewing emerging risks, the starting point is the same: what matters to us right now? From there, you can move into Explorer to examine the intelligence behind a threat. Figure 1: Prioritize threats using a personalized view of the threat landscape, organizational impact, and exposure. Bring Microsoft, third-party, and your own intelligence into the same investigation A Microsoft report may explain how an actor operates. A third-party feed may identify infrastructure associated with that activity. Your own team may have intelligence from a previous investigation. Each contributes a different part of the picture. Threat Intelligence Explorer lets you work with those sources together. Microsoft Research articles and indicators sit alongside connected third-party feeds and intelligence curated by your organization. Start with what you know: an actor's name, a CVE, a domain, or an IP address. Free-text search finds matching intelligence across the types and sources available to your organization. Refine the results by type, industry, geography, or source, then follow relationships to understand how individual findings fit together. Threat Intelligence Explorer covers indicators, threat actors, campaigns, attack patterns, tools, vulnerabilities, and reports. You can move from understanding a threat to examining its associated intelligence, then continue from an indicator's details into the relevant Defender entity page for deeper investigation. Figure 2: Search across intelligence sources and follow relationships from a threat to the evidence you need to investigate. Follow a lead from relevance to investigation Suppose your team is researching Aqua Blizzard . The question is not simply what the actor does, but whether its activity should change your priorities. In Threat Intelligence Overview, you can review threats relevant to your industry and regions alongside available impact and exposure information. In Threat Intelligence Explorer, a search for the actor brings together matching intelligence from Microsoft, your connected feeds, and your organization's repository. From there, you can review a report, filter the results, and follow available relationships to associated intelligence. If an indicator warrants a closer look, continue into its Defender entity page to investigate further. As the picture becomes clearer, you can tag relevant records in your Threat Intelligence Platform and curate intelligence for the team. What began as a question about a threat actor becomes focused research, a deeper investigation where needed, and intelligence your colleagues can build on. Keep the intelligence you rely on Threat Intelligence Overview and Explorer replace the previous Threat Intelligence pages (Threat Analytics, Intel Management) with a personalized starting point and a shared investigation workspace. The Microsoft reports you rely on remain available in full detail (build on convergence of Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence into Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR ), and your existing intelligence carries over. The transition is designed to preserve existing threat intelligence capabilities, with the new experience bringing them together through Threat Intelligence Overview and Explorer. Customers with an eligible Microsoft Defender license can access the new experience . For details on eligible licenses, see Microsoft Defender XDR prerequisites .
